title: I Took the Bookbinding Nipping-Press Booking to the Mentor Who Left My Signatures

parts.text: I opened press two at 2:06 p.m. and mentor Ivo was already nipping my numbered signatures. The slate said: ONE PRESS. SIXTY MINUTES. SIGNATURES STAY WITH THE BOOKING. I was forty-four, bindery member, holding a sewing card that listed our text. Ivo shrugged. "Mentors are the press." I photographed the slate, the booking, and his boards on my stack. Then I asked for the press log. At 2:14 the studio pinged why Ivo's name was on my signatures. I kept my voice bindery-soft and let the timestamp talk. A slate is only a slate until someone treats it like a clock.
parts.cliffhanger_hint: The studio can see Ivo's boards on my stack during our booking.

social.video_title: He nipped my numbered signatures on my press — Part 1/2
social.description: Nipping press, a mentor on my stack, a sixty-minute slate he posted. I logged the boards. Would you have asked for the press log?

parts.text: Ivo called it a squeeze until the studio asked for the photo. I printed the ticket, the slate, and the boards still. The signatures went back to my press. Ivo ran his own sixty and told the next mentor atmosphere was always about square. Square is a word mentors use when a booking exists. Press policy now has a second line: MENTORS ARE NOT THE PRESS. I keep our text on a labeled board. Ivo brown-bags his jokes. The bindery finally looks like a booking, not a loan. The rule looks ordinary now, which is the whole point.

social.video_title: Mentors are not the press — Part 2/2
social.description: Press log, numbered signatures, and a second line on the slate. Was a squeeze ever my stack?
